stories.title: Odisha CM announces special package for families affected by Cyclone Arnab
stories.summary: After reviewing the prevailing flood situation in the State in the evening, CM Majhi said people in several districts, especially Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal, were affected by cyclone Arnab and its aftermath of heavy rainfall
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi on Sunday (October 2, 2026) announced a special package of 50kg of rice and ₹2,500 for every family affected by the recent rain and flood in the southern districts, besides damages for losses to crops and property due to Cyclone Arnab.
With another cyclonic storm expected to hit the coasts of Andhra Pradesh, the Chief Minister said the relief package will be reviewed again upon assessing damage after the weather system passes.

After reviewing the prevailing flood situation in the State in the evening, CM Majhi said people in several districts, especially Ganjam, Gajapati and Kandhamal, were affected by cyclone Arnab and its aftermath of heavy rainfall.

“Thousands of acres of crops and several houses have been damaged,” he told reporters and pointed out that assessment of damage was underway while the primary task was relief distribution and restoration.
"I am hopeful that normalcy will return in affected areas in the next one or two days as the administration is taking all necessary measures," he said.
The Chief Minister announced that all affected families will get 50kg of rice and ₹2,500 in cash.

Small and marginal farmers, who sustained crop loss of 33% and above, will receive an agricultural input subsidy of ₹8,500 per hectare of land in rain-fed and non-irrigated areas, while ₹17,000 per hectare of land will be provided for areas under assured irrigation, he said.

Similarly, assistance for perennial crops like mango and cashew will be ₹22,500 per hectare, the Chief Minister said, adding that a minimum agricultural input subsidy of ₹2500 will be given to any affected farmer for perennial crops and ₹1000 for non-irrigated areas.
"The government will provide ₹18,000 to each affected farmer to remove sand and silt from the fields.
The State will also provide 1.75 lakh mini kits to farmers for free," he added.

Under the housing sector, he said assistance of ₹1.20 lakh will be given for fully damaged houses in the plains, ₹1.30 lakh in hilly areas, while ₹6,500 and ₹4,000 will be given for partially damaged pucca and kutcha houses, respectively.
CM Majhi said his government has decided to provide compensation of ₹10,000 for affected small shops, street vendors and kiosks and ₹25,000 for affected big shops and commercial establishments.

article_sentences: Observing that having a mere criminal antecedent would not be definitive proof of guilt, the Supreme Court recently granted bail to a man who had five similar criminal antecedents and was accused of procuring 23 kg of cow meat and storing it in an open plot for retail sale purposes.

A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice Vipul M. Pancholi allowed the appeal filed by Mohammad Aarif Abdul Razak Samol, who had been arrested on January 3, 2026, and remained in custody for more than eight months.
The appellant was booked under Sections 5(1), 6(b), 8(2), 8(4) and 10 of the Gujarat Animal Preservation Act, 2011, Section 325 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), and Section 119 of the Gujarat.
Police Act.
The prosecution alleged that he had illegally procured 23 kg of cow meat, transported it in a Swift car, and stored it in an open plot near his house for retail sale.
It was further alleged that he fled from the spot after the police conducted a raid.
Opposing bail, the State submitted that the trial was at its final stage and would be concluded within two months.
It also pointed out that the appellant had five criminal antecedents involving similar allegations and argued that he was likely to indulge in similar activities if released.
The appellant, however, contended that the prosecution case was based entirely on circumstantial evidence and presumptions.
His counsel submitted that he had not been arrested at the spot, the meat had been recovered from an open plot accessible to everyone, and the plot did not belong to him.
It was also argued that the Swift car allegedly used for transporting the meat was not owned by the appellant.

Finding that the appellant's continued incarceration was not warranted, the Court noted that the alleged meat had been recovered from an open plot near his house, the charge-sheet had been filed and the trial had already commenced.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(November 2) refused to interfere with the Delhi High Court's order declining to stay the conviction and sentence of conman Sukesh Chandrashekhar pending appeal.

He was recently convicted and sentenced under Sections 170(Personating a Public Servant), 189(Threat of Injury to a Public Servant) and 507(Criminal Intimidation by Anonymous Communication) of the Indian Penal Code for impersonating a Supreme Court Judge and attempting to pressurise a judicial officer to grant bail.

Chandrashekhar had allegedly impersonated the private secretary of a sitting Supreme Court Judge and subsequently the Judge himself, making calls to a judicial officer in an attempt to secure favourable orders in his case.

The allegation against Sukesh was that while in police custody in connection with a 2017 corruption case he obtained access to a constable's mobile phone in whose custody he was and thereafter used it to contact the official landline and mobile number of the judicial officer who was presiding over the corruption case.
On August 20, the Chief Judicial Magistrate convicted him, and on August 29, sentenced him to imprisonment.

Against this, he approached the Additional Sessions Judge and then the Delhi High Court for staying his conviction and sentence under Section 528 read with Section 430(2) of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023.
The challenge was primarily against the strong observations made by the Trial Court regarding the conduct attributed to Chandrashekhar while recording his conviction.
However, both Courts dismissed his plea, with the High Court stating that this must be examined by the Court hearing his appeal and not at this stage.
The matter was taken up before a bench comprising Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice Manmohan.
Justice Pardiwala questioned Senior Advocate Shoeb Alam (for Suresh) as to why he wants a stay on the conviction.
Alam stated that observations were made because he has 31 pending criminal antecedents against him.
He stated that the observations were made despite the Trial Court itself noting that he has not been convicted in these cases.

stories.headline: Cold grips Delhi as air quality slips to very poor levels
stories.title: Cold grips Delhi as air quality slips to very poor levels
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 2 : Delhi-NCR residents experienced a wintry chill on Monday morning, with winter gradually setting in across the region. Meanwhile, the air quality fell to the 'very poor’ category, with the overall Air Quality Index (AQI) recorded at 310 after a few days' respite because of the rain last week. Several monitoring stations across the national Capital and its surrounding areas reported 'poor' to 'very poor' air quality. The AQI stood at 313 in Burari, 258 in Badarpur, 213 in Chhawla, 237 in Jharoda Kalan, 273 in Vasundhara Enclave, 256 in Karala and 310 in Uttam Nagar. Other areas also recorded high pollution levels, including Ghoga at 274, Nangloi at 319, NIH Narela at 353, Mandir Marg at 340, Aya Nagar at 288, CRRI Mathura Road at 334 and Pusa at 340. Sirifort recorded an AQI of 354, while Chandni Chowk stood at 361 and Burari Crossing at 354. The AQI was also recorded at 319 in JNU, 382 in Alipur, 359 at North Campus, Delhi University, 322 at Talkatora Garden and 357 at Dwarka Sector-8. As northern India begins to experience the onset of winter, the country is witnessing a sharp contrast in weather conditions. While northern states are enjoying pleasant weather and cooler temperatures, southern and eastern regions are preparing for heavy rainfall amid the approach of Cyclone Murasu towards the Andhra Pradesh coast. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Delhi is expected to witness a bright day, with temperatures ranging between 17 degrees Celsius and 29 degrees Celsius. No rainfall warning has been issued for the national Capital. Punjab and Haryana are also expected to remain largely dry, providing residents with some respite from unpredictable weather conditions. Meanwhile, the Bay of Bengal is witnessing increased weather activity, with Cyclone Murasu expected to intensify before approaching the Andhra Pradesh coast. Winter conditions are also tightening their grip on Himalayan destinations, including Spiti, Ladakh and Kedarnath. To tackle rising pollution during the winter months, the Delhi government has begun enforcing fixed-term restrictions under its Winter Action Plan from November 1. The measures will remain in force for varying periods until February 28. A complete ban on construction and demolition activities, except for specified exemptions, will be imposed from December 10 to January 20. The plan aims to curb vehicular emissions, control dust and reduce road traffic during the peak winter season. The government has also staggered office timings to ease traffic congestion. Delhi government offices will function from 10 a.m. to 6:30 p.m., while Municipal Corporation of Delhi offices will operate from 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. until February 28. Parking charges at authorised municipal sites will also be doubled to discourage the use of private vehicles. On the first day of the Winter Action Plan, authorities imposed penalties and environmental compensation totalling Rs 68.4 lakh. Enforcement teams checked nearly 15,000 vehicles, turned back 1,539 at border points and issued 566 challans for violations of Pollution Under Control Certificate norms. According to official data available till 5 p.m. on Sunday, penalties included Rs 56.6 lakh for PUCC violations, Rs 2 lakh for breaches of vehicle entry restrictions and Rs 9.8 lakh as environmental compensation for violations of dust-control norms at construction and demolition sites. --IANS

stories.headline: Six Indian tourists safely rescued From snow-hit Nepal's Dolpa
stories.title: Six Indian tourists safely rescued From snow-hit Nepal's Dolpa
stories.summary: Kathmandu, Nov 2 : Six Indian tourists, stranded in the upper reaches of the remote Dolpa district in western Nepal amid heavy snowfall, were safely rescued by helicopter on Monday morning, a senior police officer in the district said. The Indian tourists had been out of contact since October 31 because of snowfall in the area. "A helicopter was deployed after they were located, and they were brought to the district headquarters, Dunai," Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) Anil Raj Giri, chief of the District Police Office in Dolpa, told IANS. He said the health conditions of all six rescued tourists were normal. DSP Giri said the tourists were rescued from the Danigadh area of Shey-Phoksundo Rural Municipality after being caught in severe weather conditions. The group encountered heavy snowfall while trekking from Dho Tarap towards Shey-Phoksundo Lake, a popular tourist destination. Upon receiving information about the stranded tourists on October 31, authorities launched efforts to rescue them, officials told local media. However, they said that the operation was delayed because of adverse weather conditions and difficulties in arranging a helicopter. According to DSP Giri, the Indian tourists had reached Upper Dolpa without obtaining the required administrative permits. The Department of Immigration is responsible for issuing trekking permits to foreign nationals visiting restricted areas in the upper part of the district. Giri asserted local authorities had warned the tourists against travelling in the area because of worsening weather conditions linked to Cyclone Arnab in the Bay of Bengal. On October 27, Nepal's Department of Immigration suspended the issuance of trekking permits for restricted areas in the high hills and Himalayan regions for October 29–31, citing a high risk of heavy snowfall, snowstorms and avalanches. The decision followed a warning from the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority urging tourists to avoid travelling to these areas during the three days. The authority separately had advised tourists to take precautions, warning that road and air transport services and other aspects of daily life could be disrupted. It had also urged people to avoid non-essential travel during the period. --IANS

stories.headline: Gujarat orders schools with 100+ students to hire counsellors
stories.title: Gujarat orders schools with 100+ students to hire counsellors
stories.summary: Gandhinagar, Nov 2: All secondary and higher secondary schools in Gujarat will have to set up dedicated teams to monitor students' mental health and prevent suicides under new regulations introduced by the state government, with schools having 100 or more students required to appoint at least one qualified counsellor. The provisions, which will apply to students of Classes 9 to 12 in schools affiliated with the Gujarat Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Board (GSHSEB), seek to address growing concerns over academic pressure, examination-related anxiety, social media use, family expectations and other factors affecting students' mental well-being. The Education Department has introduced Regulation 16(A) in the Gujarat Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Regulations, 1974, and incorporated detailed provisions in Appendix 8 covering mental health, student welfare and suicide prevention. "The decision was taken under the guidance of Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, Education Minister Pradyuman Vaja and Minister of State for Education, Rivaba Jadeja," officials said. It follows a Supreme Court judgment laying down 15 binding guidelines and four directives on students' mental health and suicide prevention in educational institutions. The Union Ministry of Law and Justice had instructed states to implement the directions. The state has also adopted the UMMEED guidelines developed by the National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT) as a reference framework. UMMEED stands for Understand, Motivate, Manage, Empathise, Empower and Develop. Under the new regulations, every school offering Classes 9 to 12 must constitute a School Wellness Team (SWT) at the beginning of each academic year. The team will be responsible for identifying students experiencing mental distress, responding to suicide risks and ensuring timely access to support. Its functioning will be reviewed annually. The school principal will lead the team, while the school counsellor or a designated teacher will serve as its coordinator. It will also include one teacher each from the secondary and higher secondary sections, a School Management Committee representative, a non-teaching staff member and two student peer leaders, known as 'Mano-Mitra', with one each from Classes 9-10 and 11-12. The Mano-Mitra initiative will establish a peer-support system within schools. These student representatives will provide initial emotional support to classmates, guide those requiring help towards appropriate assistance and encourage supportive relationships among students. stories.title: Karnataka issues final land acquisition notification for Greater Bengaluru township

article_sentences: The Karnataka government has issued the final land acquisition notification for 1,895 acres in Kanchugaranahalli and Byramangala villages of Bidadi Hobli in Ramanagara taluk for the proposed Greater Bengaluru Integrated Township (GBIT).

The October 30 notification identifies 3,271 landowners whose compensation will be determined under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013.
Landowners can also opt for developed sites in lieu of monetary compensation.
The Greater Bengaluru Development Authority (GBDA), which is implementing the project, plans to develop the township under a ‘work-live-play’ model.
The proposed township is planned across villages between Bidadi and Harohalli in Bengaluru South district.
It has faced sustained opposition from farmers and local residents for over a year, who fear losing agricultural land and their livelihoods.
Earlier in August, the state government constituted a four-member committee headed by Justice Guhanathan Narendar to examine the differing views on the Bidadi Township project.
The committee was tasked with examining the project’s legal, humanitarian, and developmental aspects and submitting its recommendations to the government.
Farmers in the affected villages said they would continue opposing the acquisition.

Nagaraj MR of the Byramangala and Kanchugaranahalli Farmers’ Land Rights Protection Association said the final notification was issued even before a government-appointed review committee submitted its report.
Nagaraj also alleged that farmers were threatened with litigation and pressured to accept compensation and give up their land.

The township proposal received Cabinet approval in January 2025, following which the GBDA issued a preliminary land acquisition notification in March 2025, proposing to acquire 7,481 acres across nine villages.

stories.title: US tariff waiver on Russia-linked oil purchases to boost India-US trade: Report
stories.summary: The report from Times Kuwait said the Executive Order signed by President Donald Trump recently could boost bilateral trade momentum, support employment and advance the $500 billion India–US bilateral trade ambition by 2030.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The report from Times Kuwait said the Executive Order signed by President Donald Trump recently could boost bilateral trade momentum, support employment and advance the $500 billion India–US bilateral trade ambition by 2030.

New Delhi: The United States' decision to waive Russia-linked tariff and sanctions measures on major buyers of Russian-origin oil and gas could provide significant relief to Indian exporters, restore business confidence and help accelerate bilateral trade, a new report has said.
The order eased the immediate threat of additional tariffs of up to 100 per cent on Indian exports linked to Russian energy purchases, reducing uncertainty for businesses.
Businesses gain more room to plan shipments, negotiate contracts, and make investment decisions with greater confidence.
Engineering goods and industrial machinery exports rely on long-term procurement relationships, competitive pricing and reliable delivery schedules.

US importers can assess Indian sourcing options without the same immediate concern, the report said, adding that businesses on both sides can focus more on expanding commercial opportunities rather than on responding to successive policy uncertainties.

"Although the waiver does not eliminate every tariff-related challenge, it reduces the risk of further escalation in trade tensions and provides an opportunity to rebuild momentum in one of India’s most important export markets," the report noted.
The United States remains India’s largest destination for merchandise exports, comprising manufacturing, pharmaceuticals, engineering, electronics and labour-intensive goods.
India’s merchandise exports to the US rose from about $86.5 billion in FY25 to $87.3 billion in FY26, up about 0.9 per cent despite tariff measures during the year.
Exports in September 2026 rose to $8.02 billion, up 48 per cent from $5.42 billion in September 2025.

“Greater coordination on energy, manufacturing, technology, investment and supply chains can help both countries identify shared interests and reduce the risk of future disruptions,” the report noted.

stories.headline: Third AAP MLA resigns in two days as Kunwar Vijay Pratap quits
stories.title: Third AAP MLA resigns in two days as Kunwar Vijay Pratap quits
stories.summary: Chandigarh, Nov 2 : In a major development in Punjab's ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP), Amritsar North MLA, Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, resigned on Monday, following in the footsteps of two other MLAs who resigned the previous day. Singh, a former IPS officer, also sent his resignation letter to the Punjab Assembly Speaker on Monday. He was suspended by the AAP for five years in June 2025 for alleged anti-party activities as he had opposed the arrest of Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) leader Bikram Singh Majithia in a Disproportionate Assets case. Sharing the information on X, Singh said that he will remain "indebted to you until my last breath for the love and respect you have shown me", referring to the people of the state. "With your cooperation and the blessings of the Almighty, we must all unite in a collective effort to rise above the politics of lanes and ribbon-cutting, and transform Punjab—trapped by drugs, extortion, gangsterism, and corruption—back into a progressive and beloved state," he said. Singh asserted that he had achieved "90 per cent targets", adding that his "greatest achievement" is "ending the 'mai-baap' culture in politics and working by considering the public as my source of inspiration". "In the Punjab Legislative Assembly, I always raised the voice of Amritsaris and boldly addressed issues from water and sewage to Circuit House, Company Bagh, dirty drains, Guru Nanak Dev University, Government Medical College, Saroop Rani College, and the Bargari sacrilege case. This was the first time that area-specific issues were raised by me in the Punjab Legislative Assembly by naming lanes and neighbourhoods," he said. "Working together with you to formulate a forward strategy, my aim will be to ensure clean politics and transparent administration. My sole purpose is 'Punjab First'. Apart from this, I will have no personal interests," he added. Earlier on Sunday, Singh had hit out at AAP National Convener Arvind Kejriwal and Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann, asserting that the party had strayed from its founding ideals. Pratap's exit follows the resignations of fellow MLAs, Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra and Chetan Singh Jouramajra, who resigned from the AAP's primary membership and the Assembly on Sunday. Pathanmajra, who represents the Sanour Assembly constituency in Patiala district, sent his resignation letter to Arvind Kejriwal, announcing his decision to quit the party with immediate effect. Pathanmajra has been at the centre of several controversies in the past. A rape case was registered against him, following which he travelled to Australia. He was subsequently arrested by the police after returning to India to join the investigation into the case. Meanwhile, Jouramajra, who represents the Samana Assembly constituency and has also served as a minister in the Punjab government, announced his resignation through a social media post. According to media reports, tensions had reportedly been building between him and the party leadership after the AAP high command appointed former senior Shiromani Akali Dal leader Surjit Singh Rakhra as the in-charge of the Samana Assembly constituency. The decision had reportedly left Jouramajra unhappy with the party leadership, as the appointment of another leader as constituency in-charge in his own Assembly seat was viewed as a setback to his political standing and influence in the area. The resignations come at a crucial time for the AAP, which is facing a political challenge ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. --IANS
